article_text:
Films and events

Journey

A Place to Heal

Cédric Kahn’s watchful drama deftly captures life within an adolescent psychiatric unit, from the carers’ work to the kids’ trauma, friendships and lust for life.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Cédric Kahn

Screenwriters Cédric Kahn, Kahina Le Querrec

With Zoé Monpart, Malou Khebizi, Kenji Peyran

France 2026. 105min

Courtesy of Charades

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

When 17-year-old Lucia is brought to the ward, she already knows everyone. It’s not her first time there, but the arrival of a mysterious young man threatens the fragile equilibrium of the unit. Combining documentary-style observations with a lyrical third act, alongside moving performances from its mostly non-professional young cast, A Place to Heal pays homage to those precious places that offer space to heal.

Laure Bonville

Content advice

Contains scenes of sex.

Contains themes of domestic violence or abuse, self harm, and suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lemonade

Barry Keoghan plays a social worker trying to make up for the past in this heartfelt coming-of-age Irish drama about second chances.

FLORID

In this striking British feature debut, a young man living in supported accommodation tries to juggle his musical aspirations and mental health issues.

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

article_text:
9月上旬、ロンドン在住のフェイイ・ウェンによる初写真集 『butterflies are quicker than rock』 （torch press）が刊行される。本書の刊行を記念し9月12日〜20日、渋谷・(PLACE) by methodで刊行記念展覧会が開催される。会期中は作家が来日し、トークイベントやサイン会なども開催される予定だ。

写真集『butterflies are quicker than rock』でウェンは、東洋思想を手がかりに、生態系の脆さと時間の儚さを見つめている。タイトルは移ろうものと永続するもののあいだの緊張を表し、危ういバランスにある今の生態系を象徴している。大英図書館でレファレンス司書として働くかたわら、自然や風景を主題に自身の撮影したイメージと、ときにはファウンドフォトのイメージを使いながら作品を作り出している。ウェンの作品の特徴はその制作方法にあり、伝統的なプリント技法や新しい現像技法を組み合わせ、スキャンや加工、再撮影、プリントを重ねることで、色褪せた風合いや複雑なレイヤーを生み出し、風景の質感を映し出している。それらを組み合わせて構成することで、写真は固定された記録から、記憶やアーカイブが物語を紡ぎ直す流動的な対話へと変わっていく――自然のモチーフや風景は、伝統的な中国の山水画のようでありながら、幾層ものレイヤーが加えられることで、新しい風景として立ち現れていく。そして、風景を見ることとはどういうことかを、私たちに問いかける。

9月12日には、ウェンと河内タカによるトークイベントも行われるので、予定を合わせてぜひ足を運びたい。

タイトル

フェイイ・ウェン「butterflies are quicker than rock」

場所

(PLACE) by method（150-0011 東京都渋谷区東1-3-1 カミニート#14）

会期

2026年9月12日（土）〜20日（日） ＊オープニングレセプション 9月12日（土）17:30〜19:00 作家によるサイン会も開催します

時間

12:00〜19:00

イベント

トークイベント 9月12日（土）16:00〜17:15 フェイイ・ウェン×河内タカ 参加費：500円 https://correctingthewind.peatix.com/

定休日

なし

企画

article_text:
Emmy Award-winning actor and writer Richard Gadd , multi-Emmy and SAG nominated actor Bill Camp and Oscar-nominated filmmaker and actor Ray McKinnon are joining “ Rode to Ruin ,” a Western thriller directed by Michael Keaton .

Keaton also stars in the film, which is now in production in Santa Fe, New Mexico, along with Morgan Freeman and Laura Linney. Angel acquired worldwide rights and will release “Rode to Ruin” in theaters in 2027.

Related Stories

As Uncensored Re-Release of Ken Russell's 'The Devils' Shocks Audiences, Director's Son Preps Doc Feature 'Mad Dad' (EXCLUSIVE)

Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues

Also joining the cast are Chris Candy, Travis Hammer, Thom Rivera and Derek Hinkey.

“Richard, Ray and Bill are the kind of actors who make every scene better simply by being in it,” said producer Lori McCreary. “They each bring such specificity, humanity and truth to their work, and seeing them alongside Michael, Morgan and Laura is incredibly exciting. Avy Kaufman has helped us make this cast something very special.”

The story follows a retired U.S. Marshal whose 40-year search for his wife’s killer leads him to an aging outlaw losing his memory, and to a buried truth neither man may survive, according to the synopsis.

Gadd plays Clive McKinney, the young, dangerous, and charismatic head of an outlaw gang riding the territory in search of a rumored fortune and the man who destroyed his family.

“Rode to Ruin” is produced by McCreary, Keaton, Kelly Mendelsohn, Gary Lucchesi and Richard Gray for Freeman and McCreary’s Revelations Entertainment and Keaton’s George and Leona Productions.

R. Dean McCreary wrote the screenplay, and executive producers include Steve Sarowitz, Carter Boehm, Skip Herman, Blake Johnson, Randall Emmett and John Bommarito.

Gadd is represented by UTA, Individual Artist Management and Casarotto and Markham, Froggatt & Irwin. Camp is represented by UTA and Franklin, Weinrib, Rudell & Vassallo, P.C. McKinnon is represented by Paradigm, Anonymous Content and Skrzyniarz & Mallean.

Linney is represented by CAA, Lighthouse Management + Media, and Kevin Yorn; Keaton is represented by CAA and JSSK and Morgan Freeman is represented by CAA and Sloane, Offer, Weber and Dern.

article_text:
Source: Disney

Peter Rice

Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos heaped praise on incoming chief content officer Peter Rice as he talked up the UK executive’s credentials days before he officially starts in the role.

Speaking on Tuesday’s Q3 earnings call, Sarandos said while he did not anticipate any fundamental strategy shifts to the content strategy after a fraught week for the streamer that culminated in last week’s firing of Bela Bajaria and the appointment of Rice , there was a need to for “better execution in the US”.

“There’s a lot to be excited about, but I know we can do better,” Sarandos told analysts. “I’m incredibly thrilled about Peter Rice joining as our new chief content officer. I’ve known Peter for about 15 years, and the outpouring of excitement of him coming to Netflix from across the industry and from the creative community has been nothing short of overwhelming.”

The co-CEO said Rice was “one of the really rare people in the industry who’s led TV networks, movie studios, streaming services”, hailing the former Fox and Disney executive’s creative and business acumen. “But most importantly, Peter Rice understands talent relations, and in a competitive market where creative talent have choices of where they want to work, we want Netflix to always be the place that they love to do the best work of their life, Peter is the exact right person to lead those efforts in the US and around the world,” he said. Rice officially starts on October 26.

David Fincher, whose The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth opens exclusively in Imax on November 25, is one of several high-profile talents who are not renewing their deals at the streamer alongside Stranger Things creators the Duffer Brothers, Noah Baumbach, and Shawn Levy.

Netflix has been rocked by slower engagement growth in the first half of 2026 and Sarandos and co-CEO Greg Peters acknowledged that they need to do better.

Tribute to Bela Bajaria

Sarandos paid tribute to outgoing chief content officer Bela Bajaria, saying: “Bela has an incredible decade-long run here. She led the teams through expansions of new types of content. She also did the hard work of building this incredible international team who’s been making local-for-local content around the world, which has become a great competitive differentiator for us over the last decade.”

However the co-CEO clearly sees the need to up the game in the US and cited India’s strong third quarter, as well as strong performances in South Korea and Japan, Europe and the Middle East and in particular the Nordic region, a mature market that he said was “killing it”.

Asked about theatrical strategy, he reiterated that Netflix was a streaming-first business, adding that his team looked at every film on its merits when considering theatrical releases in a way that satisfies film-loving members without harming “the view value to Netflix”.

“Our theatrical strategy has evolved to include a traditional 45-day window for a handful of films,” Sarandos said, noting that the streamer was on track to release around 30 films theatrically this year, similar to 2025. “We’re also now reporting box office, so that’s new, and it looks like we picked a good title to start with with La Bola Negra . We’re one week into reporting box office and we’re happy with it, so let’s check in again in about six months.”

Sarandos commented on the appeal of licencing deals like the current arrangement with Disney that has seen all five Ice Age films break into the streamer’s weekly top 10 chart. Such deals, like the new pact with Brazil’s Globo that includes Oscar-winner I’m Still Here , were mutually beneficial to Netflix and its partners.

Peters said he was “very pleased with the early performance” of the partnership with TF1 – the streamer’s first with a traditional broadcaster. “We certainly believe we can replicate similar results with other partners.” Asked about add-on partnerships with other subscription services, Peters said they were another way to expand the entertainment offering,” adding: “There’s nothing to announce today.”

"1897年、鹿児島に生まれ、幼いころに家族と東京に移った東郷青児は、文学や音楽、絵画に触れて育ちました。当時最先端のヨーロッパ前衛芸術に傾倒し、1915年、18歳で初個展を開催した際には未来派やキュビスムの作風を取り入れた作品を展示。翌年には画家・有島生馬の勧めで公募美術展である二科展に出品し、初入選および二科賞受賞により、新進気鋭の画家として関心を呼びました。1921年、24歳で留学を目的にパリに渡り、短期間イタリア未来派の活動に関わったほか、パブロ・ピカソらの前衛芸術家たちや現地の日本人画家たちと交流しつつ制作活動を行いました。次第に、前衛芸術運動に違和感を覚え、ルーヴル美術館でイタリア、ルネサンス美術など過去の傑作に学んだといいます。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "滞欧中、東郷は、当時ヨーロッパで広まっていた「秩序への回帰」という芸術的潮流を反映して簡潔な形体を緩やかな陰影表現で描くようになりました。帰国直後の1929年、二科展にシュルレアリスム風の作品を出品し、同世代の古賀春江や阿部金剛たちとともに「新傾向の画家」として注目を集めました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《コントラバスを弾く》1915年 油彩/カンヴァス 153.0×75.4cm ©SOMPO美術館 Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷青児はコントラバス奏者の原田潤と知り合い、その縁からドイツ留学から戻ったばかりの山田耕筰（当時：耕作）と出会いました。山田は東京フィルハーモニー会管弦楽部の指揮者を務めており、練習場所の一角をアトリエとして東郷に提供しました。当時、東郷は未来派やキュビスムなどの前衛芸術に傾倒しており、音楽の響く環境で、色彩の交響楽ともいえる絵画を描こうとしました。1915年、山田の勧めで開催した初の個展で、本作を含む22点を発表した東郷は新進画家として注目を集めました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/3-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《超現実派の散歩》1929年 油彩/カンヴァス 64.0×48.2cm ©SOMPO美術館 Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷は7年間の滞仏生活を終えて帰国した直後、1929年の第16回二科展に《Déclaration（超現実派風の散歩）》というタイトルで本作を出品し、同じくシュルレアリスムを思わせる作品を発表した古賀春江や阿部金剛らとともに「新傾向」の画家として関心を集めました。翌1930年、美術雑誌『アトリヱ』「超現実主義研究号」の誌上で、東郷は「超現実派の散歩とは、散歩のつもりで超現実主義の試運転をやった意味である」と述べています。ここには、超現実主義や「新傾向」というラベリングから一定の距離をとろうとする意図が現れています。東郷は次第に独自の作風を確立していきます。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "2章 円熟期：「青児美人」、あるいは「東郷様式」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1928年の帰国後、東郷は新しい絵画表現を模索し、シュルレアリスムを思わせる作品を描いていました。しかし、画家・藤田嗣治との壁画の共同制作や女性雑誌の表紙絵、名士の肖像画の依頼に取り組むなかで、より現実に即した表現に移行し、大型の作品においても、より親しみやすい表現で優美な女性像を描くようになります。1930年代後半にかけては、絵画制作のみで生計を立てることが難しく、女性関係の問題や心中未遂事件も重なった時期ではありますが、この間にも独自の美人画といえる作風に近づいていきました。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷の女性像は、哀愁を感じさせるまなざし、滑らかな肌の質感、曲線的な身体といった特徴をもつことから、かつて一世を風靡した竹久夢二の「夢二式美人」に倣って「青児美人」、あるいは「東郷様式」と呼ばれました。東郷は、一部のエリート層だけではなく、一般大衆の生活にも美を浸透させようと努め、多くの人々を感化する美の形を追求しました。初期に未来派やキュビスムなど前衛芸術を学んで養ったモダンな感性に、常に新しい文化やファッションを取り入れることで時代の先端を行く女性像を作り上げたといえます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/4-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《望郷》1959年 油彩/カンヴァス 116.1×90.7cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "毎日新聞社が主催する第5回日本国際美術展で一般来場者の投票による大衆賞を受賞した作品です。同展で大衆賞が設置されたのは第4回、第5回のみですが、東郷は1957年の第4回展でも受賞しており、一般での人気の高さを示しています。目を伏せた女性の表情や、しなやかな曲線美を示す肢体は、高度に理想化された「東郷様式」の女性像の典型です。滑らかな絵肌と、落ち着いた色彩による描写という点でも、本作は円熟期の代表作のひとつといえます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/5-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《黒い手袋》1933年 油彩/カンヴァス 119.2×68.2cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1934年に東京火災（現・損保ジャパン）の火災保険案内の表紙に使用された作品です。モデルは作家の宇野千代とされています。1928年にフランスから帰国した東郷は、翌年交際中の女性と心中を企て、未遂に終わったものの大きく報道されました。宇野は新聞小説の題材とするため東郷に取材を申し込み、その縁から数年間生活をともにしました。東郷と宇野は下北沢に新築したアトリエ付きの住宅に引越し、その建築費用を捻出するために、宇野は東郷の作品を自ら売りに各地へ出向いたといいます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/6-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《微風》1937年 油彩/カンヴァス 115.0×78.0cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1930年代後半から1940年代初めにかけて、東郷は円形のカンヴァスを使った作品を多く制作しており、この形状から室内に展示する上での装飾性を強く意識していたことがわかります。また、本作では風になびくピンク色のショールが軽やかさを演出し、白いドレス姿の女性の無垢な愛らしさを引き立てています。東郷は牧歌的な伝統衣装から都会的で洗練されたファッションまで西洋風の装いを巧みに取り入れることで、西洋文化への憧憬を体現するような女性像を描いて人気を博しました。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "3章 他分野での活躍：書籍の装幀、文筆活動、商業デザイン"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷は学生時代から絵画のほかに、文学、音楽など芸術諸般に広く関心を抱き、執筆した文章や挿絵を文学雑誌などに寄稿していました。フランスから帰国した後には、画家として活動する一方、生活難をきっかけに多くの書籍の装幀、小説や随筆の寄稿、外国文学の翻訳などを手がけました。1929年、東郷は意中の女性と心中を図ったのち『婦人公論』に手記を寄稿したほか、この心中未遂事件について作家の宇野千代が取材に訪れたのをきっかけに関係が深まり、宇野の著書の装幀や創刊誌のロゴデザインを手がけています。また、東郷はフランスでデパートの装飾美術部に勤務した経験をもち、国内でも企業の広告部に勤めるなど、商業デザインにも関わっています。1930年代前半には、東京火災が保険案内パンフレットやポスターなどに、後身の安田火災は毎年顧客に配布するカレンダーに東郷の作品を使っていました。加えて、1950年代頃には全国各地の和洋菓子店で東郷による愛らしい女性の絵をあしらった包装紙やクッキー缶などが使用され、幅広い年齢層に「東郷様式」が浸透するようになりました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/7-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児（原画）「株式会社成城アルプス 包装紙」制作年不詳 印刷/紙 ©SOMPO美術館 Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷青児の描く清楚で愛らしい女性像は、1950年代以降に数々の和洋菓子店の包装紙や紙箱、缶などのパッケージに使用され、それらの原画や大型の壁画が店舗内の装飾として展示される例が各地で見られるようになりました。人気の洋菓子店の成城アルプスでは、水彩で描いたパリの風景と女性像をあしらった青い包装紙と紙箱が使用されており、店内の販売、喫茶スペースにも東郷の作品が飾られています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/8-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "ジャン・コクトー著、東郷青児訳/東郷青児（装幀、挿絵） 『怖るべき子供たち』白水社 1930年 SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "フランスから帰国した後、東郷は絵だけで十分な収入を得ることができず、挿絵と文章の寄稿、翻訳、装幀などを多く手がけました。フランス人作家ジャン・コクトーの著作『怖るべき子供たち』では翻訳と装幀、挿絵を担当し、1930年に第1刷10,000部が白水社から出版されました。東郷による全ページ大の挿絵12点は、この非現実的ともいえる物語の登場人物を簡潔にかわいらしく描いたもので、白い用紙の本文とは異なり薄いグレーの用紙に印刷されています。東郷は主人公たちに自身の姿を見出すほどに共感し、感動したことが翻訳の原動力になったとして、「玲瓏たる1篇の詩だ。詩小説（ポエジイ ド ロマン）のもっとも傑出した一つだ」と賞賛しています。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/9-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "宇野千代著/東郷青児（装幀） 『罌粟（けし）はなぜ紅い』中央公論社 1930年 ©SOMPO美術館 Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/10-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "宇野千代著/東郷青児（装幀） 『罌粟（けし）はなぜ紅い』中央公論社 1930年 ©SOMPO美術館 Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "宇野千代が1929年から1930年にかけて「報知新聞」に連載した同名の小説をまとめたもので、東郷が装幀を手がけました。別の作家による新聞連載時の挿絵は含まず、東郷による全ページ大の挿絵一枚が入っています。本小説中でガス中毒の場面を執筆するため、宇野は当時、心中未遂事件で注目を集めていた東郷のもとに取材に訪れ、それを機に約4年間におよぶ二人の同棲生活が始まりました。1931年には、宇野の短編集『大人の絵本』が東郷による装幀と挿絵による豪華限定版で刊行され、その後も東郷は宇野の書籍等の出版に関わりました。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "コラム 素描の情趣：人物の佇まいと街の情景"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷は紙に鉛筆、コンテ、水彩などで描いたスケッチを多く残しており、それらは油彩の丁寧に作り上げた画面とは異なり、みずみずしい即興的な表現による特有の魅力をもっています。実際の人物をモデルに制作したものは、迷いのない線描でその表情を簡潔に表しており、その人物のまとう雰囲気まで写し取っています。一方で、手や顔を大きくデフォルメし、身体を抽象的な形体としてとらえたスケッチには、モダンアートへの関心が反映されており、このような表現は晩年に東郷が制作した彫刻にも共通して現れています。東郷は後年、なじみのあるヨーロッパを越えて、南米や中東など世界各地を旅し、街の情景や人々の姿を手際のよい筆致でスケッチに残しています。とくに水彩スケッチでは、のびやかで自由な鉛筆の線と明るく透明感のある水彩による色彩が際立っていますが、これは晩年に新たに試みた油彩の表現とも通じます。東郷のスケッチは写実性よりも、その場の一瞬の情景をとらえることを目的としつつ、幅広い表現上の可能性を示すものでもありました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/11-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《モンタルバンの古城》1962年 コンテ・水彩/紙 32.0×23.0cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "南仏ニースにあるモンタルバン城塞は16世紀中ごろに建造された歴史的建造物で、かつては軍港だった美しい入り江を見はるかす丘の上にあります。ここからほど近いヴィルフランシュ=シュル=メールに東郷の友人の別荘があり、本作を描いた当時、毎年のように訪れて安らぎのひとときを過ごしました。東郷はこの入り江を南仏第一の美しい海と呼び、周辺の風景をさわやかな色彩でとらえたスケッチを残しています。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "4章 晩年：遠い国々からのインスピレーション"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "東郷はフランス留学時代にヨーロッパ各地を訪れましたが、帰国後は経済的、社会的理由により海外へ出ることは稀となっていました。しかし、1961年に二科会会長・理事となった東郷は、海外の芸術家団体との交流を促進し、パリを皮切りに国際交流展に際して現地を訪問するようになりました。1967年、70歳のときには、アラブ地方とヨーロッパを巡る旅を敢行。数か月後の二科展に、中東の民族衣装をまとった人物を描いた《モロッコの娘》、《赤い砂》など3作品を出品しました。これを契機に、東郷はエジプトやアルジェリアなどの中東・北アフリカ地域をはじめ、南米などヨーロッパ以外の国々へも繰り返し足を延ばすようになります。旅先で現地の人々の暮らしや歴史、文化、大自然に触れることで、東郷は新たな創作のインスピレーションを得ました。とくに古代遺跡で目にした大規模な彫刻や壁画に強く感化され、その画風は大きな変化を遂げました。カンヴァスは大型化し、色彩は砂色を基調にモノトーンに近づきました。そして人物や建築などのモチーフを抽象化し、大胆に配置するスタイルに至るのです。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《モロッコの娘》1967年 油彩/カンヴァス 127.7×86,5cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1967年5月から7月にかけてアラブ地域とヨーロッパを旅した東郷は、両者の間に位置するモロッコの最大都市であるカサブランカを訪れました。晴れ着姿のモロッコ人の少女に出会い、その華麗な美しさに驚いたと述べています。女性はヴェールで顔を覆うのが習慣ではあるものの、その少女は特別に顔を見せてくれたといいます。同年9月の二科展には本作に加えて、ヴェールをまとったアラブ人の男性像など、旅で着想を得た人物画3点を出品しました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/13.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《王家の谷》1973年 油彩/カンヴァス 226.7×144.4cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1973年4月、東郷はエジプト各地を旅し、かつて古代都市テーベのあったルクソールを訪れました。ここには数多くの遺跡が残り、ナイル川西岸の山間にある王家の谷は、ツタンカーメン墓を含む新王国時代の王墓24基を含む岩窟墓群を擁しています。本作は裸婦を描いているものの、その頭部の形はミイラのマスクを連想させ、背景は遺構の岩壁のようにも見えます。旅から戻った東郷は、同年9月の第58回二科展に本作を出品しました。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/14.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "東郷青児《タッシリ》1974年 油彩/カンヴァス 226.5×181.5cm SOMPO美術館 ©Sompo Museum of Art, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "北アフリカの国アルジェリアの南東部にあるサハラ砂漠にタッシリ・ナジェールと呼ばれる台地があり、そこには紀元前6000年に遡る先史時代の岩面壁画が1万5000点以上残されています。1960年代後半以降、東郷はたびたびサハラ地方を訪れており、本作を描いた1974年、77歳を迎える東郷は、遊牧民のトゥアレグ族のガイドとテント生活をし、多くの動物や人物を線刻と描画で表したタッシリ・ナジェールの壁画を取材しています。"}, 26010", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
SOMPO美術館（東京都新宿区）で、「開館50周年記念 生誕130年 東郷青児展」が2027年1月9日から開催されます。

東郷は、時代を先駆けるモダンで優美な女性像を描いた絵画で一世を風靡しました。しかし同時に、「洋画家」という枠に収まらない多彩な才能の持ち主でもあり、多くの商業デザインを手がけ、SOMPO美術館の母体企業である東京火災、安田火災（現：損害保険ジャパン）に保険案内リーフレットやポスターの原画を提供しました。また、SOMPO美術館は1976年に「東郷青児美術館」の名称で開館した際、東郷から作品の提供を受けており、その後の遺族からの寄贈も含め、現在では国内最大の東郷青児コレクションを有しています。

本展では、《望郷》などの代表作をはじめ、未来派やキュビスムを取り入れた初期の前衛的な作品から晩年の大型作品まで、過去最大級となる約100点の絵画が一挙公開されます。さらに、モダンなセンスが光る本の装幀や挿絵、かわいらしいお菓子のパッケージなど、関連資料約100点もあわせて展示されます。絵画から商業美術まで、時代を軽やかに駆け抜けた東郷青児。その知られざる全貌と色あせない魅力を「再発見」する展覧会です。

開館50周年記念 生誕130年 東郷青児展

会場：SOMPO美術館（東京都新宿区西新宿1-26-1）

会期：2027年1月9日（土）～2月21日（日）

開館時間：10:00-18:00（金曜日は20:00まで）※最終入場は閉館30分前まで

休館日：月曜日（ただし1/11は開館）、1/12

観覧料：一般（26歳以上）1,600円（1,500円）、25歳以下 1,100円（1,000円）、高校生以下無料 ※（ ）は事前購入券。事前購入券の販売は12月9日(水)から ※身体障がい者手帳・療育手帳・精神障がい者保健福祉手帳（ミライロIDも可）をご提示のご本人とその介助者1名は無料、被爆者健康手帳をご提示の方はご本人のみ無料 ※25歳以下の方は入場時に生年月日が確認できるものを要提示 ※収蔵品コーナー フィンセント・ファン・ゴッホ《ひまわり》も観覧可

アクセス：新宿駅西口より徒歩5分

詳細は、 SOMPO美術館公式サイト まで。

展覧会構成

1章 初期：ヨーロッパ前衛芸術の探究

1897年、鹿児島に生まれ、幼いころに家族と東京に移った東郷青児は、文学や音楽、絵画に触れて育ちました。当時最先端のヨーロッパ前衛芸術に傾倒し、1915年、18歳で初個展を開催した際には未来派やキュビスムの作風を取り入れた作品を展示。翌年には画家・有島生馬の勧めで公募美術展である二科展に出品し、初入選および二科賞受賞により、新進気鋭の画家として関心を呼びました。1921年、24歳で留学を目的にパリに渡り、短期間イタリア未来派の活動に関わったほか、パブロ・ピカソらの前衛芸術家たちや現地の日本人画家たちと交流しつつ制作活動を行いました。次第に、前衛芸術運動に違和感を覚え、ルーヴル美術館でイタリア、ルネサンス美術など過去の傑作に学んだといいます。

滞欧中、東郷は、当時ヨーロッパで広まっていた「秩序への回帰」という芸術的潮流を反映して簡潔な形体を緩やかな陰影表現で描くようになりました。帰国直後の1929年、二科展にシュルレアリスム風の作品を出品し、同世代の古賀春江や阿部金剛たちとともに「新傾向の画家」として注目を集めました。

東郷青児はコントラバス奏者の原田潤と知り合い、その縁からドイツ留学から戻ったばかりの山田耕筰（当時：耕作）と出会いました。山田は東京フィルハーモニー会管弦楽部の指揮者を務めており、練習場所の一角をアトリエとして東郷に提供しました。当時、東郷は未来派やキュビスムなどの前衛芸術に傾倒しており、音楽の響く環境で、色彩の交響楽ともいえる絵画を描こうとしました。1915年、山田の勧めで開催した初の個展で、本作を含む22点を発表した東郷は新進画家として注目を集めました。

東郷は7年間の滞仏生活を終えて帰国した直後、1929年の第16回二科展に《Déclaration（超現実派風の散歩）》というタイトルで本作を出品し、同じくシュルレアリスムを思わせる作品を発表した古賀春江や阿部金剛らとともに「新傾向」の画家として関心を集めました。翌1930年、美術雑誌『アトリヱ』「超現実主義研究号」の誌上で、東郷は「超現実派の散歩とは、散歩のつもりで超現実主義の試運転をやった意味である」と述べています。ここには、超現実主義や「新傾向」というラベリングから一定の距離をとろうとする意図が現れています。東郷は次第に独自の作風を確立していきます。

2章 円熟期：「青児美人」、あるいは「東郷様式」

1928年の帰国後、東郷は新しい絵画表現を模索し、シュルレアリスムを思わせる作品を描いていました。しかし、画家・藤田嗣治との壁画の共同制作や女性雑誌の表紙絵、名士の肖像画の依頼に取り組むなかで、より現実に即した表現に移行し、大型の作品においても、より親しみやすい表現で優美な女性像を描くようになります。1930年代後半にかけては、絵画制作のみで生計を立てることが難しく、女性関係の問題や心中未遂事件も重なった時期ではありますが、この間にも独自の美人画といえる作風に近づいていきました。

東郷の女性像は、哀愁を感じさせるまなざし、滑らかな肌の質感、曲線的な身体といった特徴をもつことから、かつて一世を風靡した竹久夢二の「夢二式美人」に倣って「青児美人」、あるいは「東郷様式」と呼ばれました。東郷は、一部のエリート層だけではなく、一般大衆の生活にも美を浸透させようと努め、多くの人々を感化する美の形を追求しました。初期に未来派やキュビスムなど前衛芸術を学んで養ったモダンな感性に、常に新しい文化やファッションを取り入れることで時代の先端を行く女性像を作り上げたといえます。

毎日新聞社が主催する第5回日本国際美術展で一般来場者の投票による大衆賞を受賞した作品です。同展で大衆賞が設置されたのは第4回、第5回のみですが、東郷は1957年の第4回展でも受賞しており、一般での人気の高さを示しています。目を伏せた女性の表情や、しなやかな曲線美を示す肢体は、高度に理想化された「東郷様式」の女性像の典型です。滑らかな絵肌と、落ち着いた色彩による描写という点でも、本作は円熟期の代表作のひとつといえます。

1934年に東京火災（現・損保ジャパン）の火災保険案内の表紙に使用された作品です。モデルは作家の宇野千代とされています。1928年にフランスから帰国した東郷は、翌年交際中の女性と心中を企て、未遂に終わったものの大きく報道されました。宇野は新聞小説の題材とするため東郷に取材を申し込み、その縁から数年間生活をともにしました。東郷と宇野は下北沢に新築したアトリエ付きの住宅に引越し、その建築費用を捻出するために、宇野は東郷の作品を自ら売りに各地へ出向いたといいます。

1930年代後半から1940年代初めにかけて、東郷は円形のカンヴァスを使った作品を多く制作しており、この形状から室内に展示する上での装飾性を強く意識していたことがわかります。また、本作では風になびくピンク色のショールが軽やかさを演出し、白いドレス姿の女性の無垢な愛らしさを引き立てています。東郷は牧歌的な伝統衣装から都会的で洗練されたファッションまで西洋風の装いを巧みに取り入れることで、西洋文化への憧憬を体現するような女性像を描いて人気を博しました。

3章 他分野での活躍：書籍の装幀、文筆活動、商業デザイン

東郷は学生時代から絵画のほかに、文学、音楽など芸術諸般に広く関心を抱き、執筆した文章や挿絵を文学雑誌などに寄稿していました。フランスから帰国した後には、画家として活動する一方、生活難をきっかけに多くの書籍の装幀、小説や随筆の寄稿、外国文学の翻訳などを手がけました。1929年、東郷は意中の女性と心中を図ったのち『婦人公論』に手記を寄稿したほか、この心中未遂事件について作家の宇野千代が取材に訪れたのをきっかけに関係が深まり、宇野の著書の装幀や創刊誌のロゴデザインを手がけています。また、東郷はフランスでデパートの装飾美術部に勤務した経験をもち、国内でも企業の広告部に勤めるなど、商業デザインにも関わっています。1930年代前半には、東京火災が保険案内パンフレットやポスターなどに、後身の安田火災は毎年顧客に配布するカレンダーに東郷の作品を使っていました。加えて、1950年代頃には全国各地の和洋菓子店で東郷による愛らしい女性の絵をあしらった包装紙やクッキー缶などが使用され、幅広い年齢層に「東郷様式」が浸透するようになりました。

東郷青児の描く清楚で愛らしい女性像は、1950年代以降に数々の和洋菓子店の包装紙や紙箱、缶などのパッケージに使用され、それらの原画や大型の壁画が店舗内の装飾として展示される例が各地で見られるようになりました。人気の洋菓子店の成城アルプスでは、水彩で描いたパリの風景と女性像をあしらった青い包装紙と紙箱が使用されており、店内の販売、喫茶スペースにも東郷の作品が飾られています。

フランスから帰国した後、東郷は絵だけで十分な収入を得ることができず、挿絵と文章の寄稿、翻訳、装幀などを多く手がけました。フランス人作家ジャン・コクトーの著作『怖るべき子供たち』では翻訳と装幀、挿絵を担当し、1930年に第1刷10,000部が白水社から出版されました。東郷による全ページ大の挿絵12点は、この非現実的ともいえる物語の登場人物を簡潔にかわいらしく描いたもので、白い用紙の本文とは異なり薄いグレーの用紙に印刷されています。東郷は主人公たちに自身の姿を見出すほどに共感し、感動したことが翻訳の原動力になったとして、「玲瓏たる1篇の詩だ。詩小説（ポエジイ ド ロマン）のもっとも傑出した一つだ」と賞賛しています。

宇野千代が1929年から1930年にかけて「報知新聞」に連載した同名の小説をまとめたもので、東郷が装幀を手がけました。別の作家による新聞連載時の挿絵は含まず、東郷による全ページ大の挿絵一枚が入っています。本小説中でガス中毒の場面を執筆するため、宇野は当時、心中未遂事件で注目を集めていた東郷のもとに取材に訪れ、それを機に約4年間におよぶ二人の同棲生活が始まりました。1931年には、宇野の短編集『大人の絵本』が東郷による装幀と挿絵による豪華限定版で刊行され、その後も東郷は宇野の書籍等の出版に関わりました。

コラム 素描の情趣：人物の佇まいと街の情景

東郷は紙に鉛筆、コンテ、水彩などで描いたスケッチを多く残しており、それらは油彩の丁寧に作り上げた画面とは異なり、みずみずしい即興的な表現による特有の魅力をもっています。実際の人物をモデルに制作したものは、迷いのない線描でその表情を簡潔に表しており、その人物のまとう雰囲気まで写し取っています。一方で、手や顔を大きくデフォルメし、身体を抽象的な形体としてとらえたスケッチには、モダンアートへの関心が反映されており、このような表現は晩年に東郷が制作した彫刻にも共通して現れています。東郷は後年、なじみのあるヨーロッパを越えて、南米や中東など世界各地を旅し、街の情景や人々の姿を手際のよい筆致でスケッチに残しています。とくに水彩スケッチでは、のびやかで自由な鉛筆の線と明るく透明感のある水彩による色彩が際立っていますが、これは晩年に新たに試みた油彩の表現とも通じます。東郷のスケッチは写実性よりも、その場の一瞬の情景をとらえることを目的としつつ、幅広い表現上の可能性を示すものでもありました。

南仏ニースにあるモンタルバン城塞は16世紀中ごろに建造された歴史的建造物で、かつては軍港だった美しい入り江を見はるかす丘の上にあります。ここからほど近いヴィルフランシュ=シュル=メールに東郷の友人の別荘があり、本作を描いた当時、毎年のように訪れて安らぎのひとときを過ごしました。東郷はこの入り江を南仏第一の美しい海と呼び、周辺の風景をさわやかな色彩でとらえたスケッチを残しています。

4章 晩年：遠い国々からのインスピレーション

東郷はフランス留学時代にヨーロッパ各地を訪れましたが、帰国後は経済的、社会的理由により海外へ出ることは稀となっていました。しかし、1961年に二科会会長・理事となった東郷は、海外の芸術家団体との交流を促進し、パリを皮切りに国際交流展に際して現地を訪問するようになりました。1967年、70歳のときには、アラブ地方とヨーロッパを巡る旅を敢行。数か月後の二科展に、中東の民族衣装をまとった人物を描いた《モロッコの娘》、《赤い砂》など3作品を出品しました。これを契機に、東郷はエジプトやアルジェリアなどの中東・北アフリカ地域をはじめ、南米などヨーロッパ以外の国々へも繰り返し足を延ばすようになります。旅先で現地の人々の暮らしや歴史、文化、大自然に触れることで、東郷は新たな創作のインスピレーションを得ました。とくに古代遺跡で目にした大規模な彫刻や壁画に強く感化され、その画風は大きな変化を遂げました。カンヴァスは大型化し、色彩は砂色を基調にモノトーンに近づきました。そして人物や建築などのモチーフを抽象化し、大胆に配置するスタイルに至るのです。

1967年5月から7月にかけてアラブ地域とヨーロッパを旅した東郷は、両者の間に位置するモロッコの最大都市であるカサブランカを訪れました。晴れ着姿のモロッコ人の少女に出会い、その華麗な美しさに驚いたと述べています。女性はヴェールで顔を覆うのが習慣ではあるものの、その少女は特別に顔を見せてくれたといいます。同年9月の二科展には本作に加えて、ヴェールをまとったアラブ人の男性像など、旅で着想を得た人物画3点を出品しました。

1973年4月、東郷はエジプト各地を旅し、かつて古代都市テーベのあったルクソールを訪れました。ここには数多くの遺跡が残り、ナイル川西岸の山間にある王家の谷は、ツタンカーメン墓を含む新王国時代の王墓24基を含む岩窟墓群を擁しています。本作は裸婦を描いているものの、その頭部の形はミイラのマスクを連想させ、背景は遺構の岩壁のようにも見えます。旅から戻った東郷は、同年9月の第58回二科展に本作を出品しました。

北アフリカの国アルジェリアの南東部にあるサハラ砂漠にタッシリ・ナジェールと呼ばれる台地があり、そこには紀元前6000年に遡る先史時代の岩面壁画が1万5000点以上残されています。1960年代後半以降、東郷はたびたびサハラ地方を訪れており、本作を描いた1974年、77歳を迎える東郷は、遊牧民のトゥアレグ族のガイドとテント生活をし、多くの動物や人物を線刻と描画で表したタッシリ・ナジェールの壁画を取材しています。

東郷青児・プロフィール

鹿児島県に生まれ、幼少期に東京へ移る。本名は鉄春。18歳のときに東郷青児の名で初個展を開催し、未来派やキュビスムを思わせる前衛的な作品で注目を集めた。翌年の第3回二科展では初入選にして二科賞を受賞する。1921年から約7年間フランスに滞在。ピカソやイタリア未来派のマリネッティらと交流するが、次第に理論重視の前衛運動から離れ、古典美術への関心を高める。また、壁画や装飾美術の制作に携わったことで、一般市民が享受できる大衆美術の重要性に開眼した。帰国後は二科展を拠点に、パリで親交のあった藤田嗣治らと活動。当時は絵画制作のみでの生活が難しく、企業の広告部などで働きながら雑誌への寄稿や挿絵も手がけた。この過程で作風は変化し、滑らかな筆致と陰影で優美な女性像を描く独自のスタイルを確立。書籍の装幀や商業美術にも広く展開されたその作品は、「東郷様式」または「青児美人」と呼ばれ、大衆の圧倒的な支持を得た。戦後は二科会の再興にいち早く着手し、運営の主導的位置に立って海外交流や新部会の設立など活動の幅を広げた。晩年には中東や南米など世界各地を歴訪し、現地の風土、文化に触発された落ち着いた色調の大型作品を描き始めるなど、生涯にわたり制作の意欲を燃やし続けた。1978年に急逝。前衛芸術から出発し、広く親しまれる美を志向しながら、昭和の美術界を力強く牽引した巨匠である。

洗練された優美な女性像「青児美人」で昭和の美術界を席巻した東郷青児ですが、その創作の軌跡は、ヨーロッパ最先端の前衛芸術への傾倒から、装幀や包装紙といった日常を彩る商業デザイン、そして晩年に広大な異国の地で挑んだモニュメンタルな大作群まで、驚くほど豊かな広がりを持っています。SOMPO美術館の開館50周年という節目の年に実現する本展は、約100点の絵画と約100点の貴重な関連資料を通じ、東京では7年ぶりとなる過去最大規模でその多彩な足跡を一望できるまたとない機会です。親しみ深い優美さの奥に秘められた、時代の先端を果敢に駆け抜けた画家の知られざる挑戦と美の全貌を、ぜひ美術館の空間で心ゆくまで体感してみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
Tokyo Art Beatでは有料会員向けの美術館割引サービス 「ミューぽん」 を、常時複数館を対象に提供している。ここでは、2026年11月に開催される「ミューぽん」対象の展覧会とその見どころを紹介！ まだサービスを使ったことのないユーザーの皆様も、ぜひ ラインアップ をチェックしてみてほしい。

3ヶ月無料の特別キャンペーン中！ 下のボタンから会員登録していただくと、3ヶ月無料で「ミューぽん」をはじめとした有料会員限定機能をお試しいただけます。

＊有料会員の 詳細はこちら （月払い300円・年払い2500円） ＊ほかの対象展覧会は こちらをチェック

「テート美術館 ターナー展──崇高の絵画、現代美術との対話」（国立西洋美術館）

英国絵画史を代表する画家、J.M.W.ターナー。本展では、テート美術館のコレクションを中心に、ターナーの作品をテーマごとに再構成し、緩やかな時系列に沿って紹介する。さらに、現代美術との対話を通して、光、自然、崇高をめぐるターナーの問題意識が、後世のアーティストたちにどのように受け継がれているのかを探る。

会場： 国立西洋美術館 会期：10月24日〜2027年2月21日 ミューぽん で200円OFF！

「テート美術館 ターナー展」が国立西洋美術館で開幕。エリアソン、ティルマンスらの現代美術と200年の時を超えて並ぶ

東京・上野の国立西洋美術館で「テート美術館 ターナー展──崇高の絵画、現代美術との対話」が開幕。世界最大のターナー・コレクションを誇るテート美術館から80点以上が集まり、オラファー・エリアソンやヴォルフガング・ティルマンスらの現代美術とともに並ぶ。会期は2027年2月21日まで

「フォンタネージ ――イタリアの光・心の風景」（三菱一号館美術館）

浅井忠ら初期洋画家を育てたイタリア人画家、アントニオ・フォンタネージの画業をたどる日本初の大回顧展。トリノ市立近現代美術館（GAM）およびトリノ博物館財団の協力のもと、画業の初期から晩年に至るまでのフォンタネージの作品群を概観する。また、日本の弟子たちの作品や、同時代・次世代のイタリア人作家の作品における彼の影響と遺産にも光を当て、フォンタネージの芸術の全貌を約200点により明らかにする。

会場： 三菱一号館美術館 会期：10月17日〜2027年1月24日 ミューぽん で100円OFF！

「フォンタネージ ――イタリアの光・心の風景」（三菱一号館美術館）レポート。日本の洋画の礎を築いたイタリア人画家の全貌をたどる

トリノ市立近現代美術館の所蔵品など約200点が集結。会期は10月17日〜2027年1月24日

「種と根っこ―都市の耕し方」（東京オペラシティ アートギャラリー）

人間の生活が自然環境を変化させる主な要因になっている現在、生態系に不安定さが生じ、自然と人工の境界はますます曖昧になりつつある。本展では、こうした都市の現状を背景に、変容を続ける自然環境との関係を結びなおそうとする制作を行う作家たちを紹介。これまで同施設で現代美術、建築、ファッションなど幅広いジャンルの展覧会を行ってきた取り組みを架橋しながら、都市における自然を新たにとらえ直す作品群が展示される。

会場： 東京オペラシティ アートギャラリー 会期：10月17日〜12月20日 ミューぽん で200円OFF！

「種と根っこ―都市の耕し方」（東京オペラシティ アートギャラリー）レポート。10人のアーティストが示す、「自然とのつながり」への多様な視点

会期は10月17日〜12月20日

「吉田璋也のデザイン― 新作民藝運動がめざした未来」（パナソニック汐留美術館）

医師でありながら、民藝のプロデューサーとして活動した吉田璋也。吉田は日常の暮らしに用いられる品を自らデザインし、生産、流通、販売の仕組みを整えながら、民藝運動に深く関わった。本展では、伝統的な手仕事を現代の生活へ根づかせるために生み出された「新作民藝」の軌跡を、作品や資料を通して紹介する。

会場： パナソニック汐留美術館 会期：10月15日～12月20日 ミューぽん で100円OFF！

「河口龍夫 関係―無関係 湖畔にて」（市原湖畔美術館）

「関係」という概念を軸に、半世紀以上にわたり現代美術の最前線で思考と制作を重ねてきた日本を代表する現代美術家・河口龍夫の展覧会。本展は、美術館の建築空間と湖畔という周辺環境に触発された新作と、房総のアトリエで制作された未発表作品を中心に紹介する。昆虫から宇宙まで、ジュラ紀から現在まで、あらゆる存在と時間に向きあい、1960年代より持続する河口の旺盛な創作欲とみずみずしい好奇心に導かれた作品世界に注目したい。

会場： 市原湖畔美術館 会期：10月17日〜12月20日 ミューぽん で100円OFF！

こちらの記事 では10月の「ミューぽん」が使えるおすすめ展覧会も公開中。開催中の展覧会も多いため、あわせてチェックしてほしい。

【割引】「ミューぽん」が使える、10月の注目の展覧会5選｜マリメッコ、「共時的星叢」展、ジョルジュ・ルオーなど

10月に開催されている「ミューぽん」対象の展覧会と、その概要を紹介する。今月は、マリメッコ展、「共時的星叢」展、水滸伝展、ボタニカル・アートとデザイン展、ジョルジュ・ルオー展の5つ

Tokyo Art Beatで長年愛されてきた展覧会チケット割引機能「ミューぽん」がより便利になりました。

title_original: Even Martin Scorsese uses AI for storyboards. Can the art survive?
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids . That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm , citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon ; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”.", "links": [{"text": "reincarnated screen icons", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/apr/16/first-trailer-released-for-ai-val-kilmer-western"}, {"text": "uncanny humanoids", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jul/11/ai-actor-tilly-norwood-movie"}, {"text": "on the board of a gen AI firm", "url": "https://stability.ai/news-updates/james-cameron-joins-stability-ai-board-of-directors"}, {"text": "recent documentary about John Lennon", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/may/16/john-lennon-last-interview-review-steven-soderbergh"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b0a5fde115c51a5fd45e9a0ec5b762b61284e164/0_0_3404_4370/master/3404.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "Storyboard by Saul Bass for Psycho, depicting the shower murder scene in sketched panels", "caption": "Meticulous … Saul Bass’ storyboard for the shower scene in Alfred Hitchcock’s Psycho Photograph: TCD/Prod.DB/Alamy", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. article_text:
A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids . That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm , citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon ; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”.

The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. Storyboards are used to work out how a film will look, and as a blueprint to communicate a director’s vision to cast and crew , and are one of the first steps in bringing a script off the page. Now they appear on the verge of replacement by programmes that use text prompts to create illustrations instead. Even an old-school diehard like Martin Scorsese has got on board; in June he announced a partnership with an AI firm whose text-to-image model he used in the storyboarding process for his next movie.

Usually, storyboards are made together by a director, an artist and other crew members responsible for the film’s visual storytelling, such as cinematographers, editors, production designers, stunt co-ordinators and more. “I find it very fulfilling to make art in such a collaborative way,” says Alex Clark , a British storyboard artist whose recent films include Bong Joon Ho’s sci-fi comedy Mickey 17 , adventure romance The Gorge and Louis Leterrier’s recent thriller The Last House . “It’s about people sitting down to discuss each other’s ideas. You might act things out, make sound effects, read dialogue. You develop a creative relationship with one another.”

For Clark, the process of creating a storyboard is just as important as the finished product. “A common misconception is that storyboarding is about making nice drawings. But it’s more than that – it’s about relating to how the director is thinking, and conceiving the most appropriate ways to tell the story of a scene,” he says. Dune director Denis Villeneuve articulated this relationship when describing his frequent collaborator, artist Sam Hudecki, as “an extension of my brain”. For Villeneuve, storyboarding is “a new way of writing”: writing a screenplay might provide the words, but storyboarding is the first step in creating the “cinematic language of the movie”. He views it as “a way to dream” as the film begins to come to life on the page.

Clark says that there is a balance that must be struck between “capturing the essence” of a scene and figuring out how the shots are going to work once the cameras are rolling. “The act of how you mark the page – to convey forms, tones, compositions, blocking and so on – forces you to thoroughly think about how all these different details will affect the scene. It gives you a rigorous understanding of how the scene is going to work.” Clark’s work reflects the fact that storyboarding is one step in an ongoing collaboration that continues through pre-production, shooting on set and beyond. “Sometimes I try to scale the drawings back, when it feels appropriate to leave space for others to build on it – whether it’s an actor’s performance, the way the set is decorated, lighting setup or subtle movement of the camera. I like finding space for happy accidents.”

For researchers and film enthusiasts, storyboard art offers a glimpse into the journey that lies behind a film, including fascinating changes in direction like this. “Storyboard art shows us the evolution of the creative vision,” says Ferdinando Cocco, a lecturer in film at Abertay university in Dundee. He points to Disney’s 1991 film Beauty and the Beast as an example: when it was first being worked on in the late 1980s, the storyboards had a rococo-inspired aesthetic , contemporary to the fairytale’s origins, styling Gaston as a bewigged 18th-century French aristocrat rather than the swollen, strong-jawed hunter who exemplified more modern ideals of masculinity.

As a film-making technique, the storyboard was first used regularly by Disney animators in the 1930s and and it plays a key role in their production process (as evidenced by displays of concept and storyboard art , and the side-by-side videos Disney posts online . (Disney also announced a $1bn investment into OpenAI’s video tool Sora last year.)

Storyboards were swiftly adopted by live-action productions, dating at least back to Gone With the Wind (1939). Since then, many film-makers have left behind storyboards that are beautiful and evocative images in themselves. Alfred Hitchcock created meticulously detailed storyboards, which spawned some of the genre’s most recognisable images: such as the shower scene in Psycho sketched beforehand by his frequent collaborator Saul Bass, the graphic designer behind many classic posters of the era. And before that, Hitchcock had worked with Salvador Dalí on surreal designs for the dream sequence in his 1945 film Spellbound.

Other directors, including Akira Kurosawa and Ridley Scott – whose storyboards are known as “Ridleygrams” – draw their own. Some of Bong’s self-drawn sketches are currently on display at the Academy Museum in Los Angeles , and his panels for Parasite have been published as a graphic novel . “Whenever I go to set without storyboards, I feel like I’m standing in the middle of Grand Central Terminal wearing only my underwear,” Bong writes in the book’s preface – however he does encourage the reader to see the differences between the storyboards and the film as “exciting moments of fear and spontaneity”.

Fan interest in behind-the-scenes material has created a market for storyboard books, while last year an exhibition devoted to storyboard art held in Milan displayed panels from films made by arthouse auteurs such as Ingmar Bergman and Federico Fellini, to artists Isaac Julien and Carrie Mae Weems, to Hollywood royalty – including Scorsese.

Creating engaging images is not without a practical function either, as storyboards are often pinned up on set to give the crew a sense of what will be shot that day. “I feel a responsibility to produce work that inspires and captivates everyone about what they’re making,” Clark says. “If the level of artistry and attention is evident at this stage, I believe it can set the tone on set, of valuing the craft involved.”

All hope is not yet lost. Cocco has observed a return to analogue practices and suggests that AI can be used in a way that fosters rather than dilutes the creative process. “Perhaps the difficulty that AI purportedly overcomes was the whole point from the start,” Cocco says. “Having to communicate with others forces an expansion of the artistic vision in ways that cannot be pre-empted.”

Clark meanwhile predicts that, as AI usage in the industry increases, people will come to have a greater appreciation for films with a human touch. “Ultimately, I think most successful films make you feel something as a human being. One advantage of hand-drawn storyboards is that you have a direct sense of that human authenticity right there on the page.”

article_text:
Er will einen riesigen Triumphbogen in Washington, doch jetzt regt sich Widerstand gegen Trumps Pläne. Woran sich die Gegner stören

US-Präsident Donald Trump schwebt ein riesiger Triumphbogen in der US-Hauptstadt vor – bekommt jetzt aber Gegenwind von Washington D.C. und dem angrenzenden Bundesstaat Virginia. Sie reichten bei Gericht eine Klage gegen die US-Regierung ein und werfen ihr laut Gerichtsdokument vor, dass der Plan bislang nicht vom US-Parlament genehmigt worden sei. Sie wollen deshalb den Bau untersagen lassen.

Trump will einen riesigen Triumphbogen errichten lassen, der größer sein soll als der berühmte Arc de Triomphe in Paris. Auch an der Höhe nehmen die Kläger Anstoß.

Der Triumphbogen soll an einem zentralen Ort der Hauptstadt entstehen. In der Nähe befindet sich das Lincoln Memorial, zudem liegt der riesige Militärfriedhof Arlington mit Hunderttausenden Gräbern nicht weit.

Der Präsident fällt in seiner zweiten Amtszeit seit Anfang 2025 immer wieder mit umstrittenen Architekturprojekten auf. So will er einen riesigen Ballsaal auf dem Gelände des Weißen Hauses errichten lassen. Als Golffan will er auch einen neuen Golfplatz in der Hauptstadt. Kritiker halten Trump Geltungssucht vor.

"卡尔·佩恩：其实我对她的故事了解不多，说实话，到现在也还是不太了解，因为我在片中演桑迪普，这条线差不多是从他遇见安娜之前一直到他去世之后，从头到尾。所以我从没去研究过她，因为这样演桑迪普更容易。然后你拍完一部电影，你会想，“好吧，就这样了。”……但我答应拍这部电影的原因，我记得自己还是洛杉矶一个年轻演员的时候，正是真人秀刚起步的日子，我好像参加过一个派对，类似颁奖礼那种，安娜也在，但她身边跟着大概四台摄像机和一大群随行人员，很明显她是在拍真人秀。但我记得我和朋友们当时就想，“哦，她是有真人秀所以她才那样表现，还是因为她有真人秀她才那样表现？”这个问题电影也没有完全回答，到我们这部电影结尾它仍是一个开放的问题。但我对她的了解就仅此而已，对吧？就是，“哦对，那就是那个真人秀里的安娜·妮可·史密斯。”所以，我看到我经纪人发来这部电影的邮件，是一句很短的剧情简介，我随便扫了一眼，然后附件是剧本。我点开剧本的时候，心里想，“哦对，我知道这个故事。这是讲那个因为谋杀安娜·妮可·史密斯而坐牢的医生。”然后我开始读剧本，我想，“这根本不是发生的事。我怎么会以为事情是这样的？”我从没跟进过这个案子之类的，但我为什么会以为事情是这样的？然后我又想，“我是不是那种读三条推文就以为自己什么都懂的人？”所以我带着这种想法读了剧本，最让我着迷的主要是桑迪普这个角色的不安全感，那种脆弱，还有那种拉扯——我记得电影里他说了五次，“我只是个注重隐私的人，过着私密的生活，”但接着做的每一个决定都与此相反，只是为了博取关注，对吧？所以，这个角色身上那种我从未演过的鲜活劲儿吸引了我。", article_text:
Following years of juggling acting and political work, supporting the likes of President Obama and NYC Mayor Mamdani, Kal Penn is back in leading man mode.

A day after wrapping his role in Gregg Araki ‘s The Decline of Fucking Western Civilization , Deadline caught up with the actor about his busy onscreen year that culminates with his portrayal of the late Anna Nicole Smith’s physician, Dr. Sandeep Kapoor, in writer/director Thane Economou’s Trust Me, I’m a Doctor , which is now playing in theaters.

“I was really fascinated mostly with the insecurity of the character of Sandeep, and the vulnerability and this push and pull between—I think five times in the movie, he says, ‘I’m just a private person, living a private life,’ but then makes every decision contrary to that, just to get attention, right?” explained Penn. “So, there was that kind of juiciness to a character that I hadn’t played before that attracted me to it.”

Watch on Deadline

Related Stories

Linda Hamilton & Abbie Cornish Board Anna Nicole Smith Pic ‘Trust Me, I’m A Doctor’; UTA, Fortitude To Launch Sales At Cannes

Kal Penn, Michael Chiklis, David Koechner, Nat Faxon, Wendi McLendon-Covey & 7 More Join Gregg Araki’s ‘The Decline Of F*cking Western Civilization’

Based on Kapoor’s 2017 memoir Trust Me, I’m A Doctor: My Life Before, During and After Anna Nicole Smith , the Economou-helmed biopic recounts the doctor’s professional relationship with Smith as his patient, which was blurred when they began a brief friendship outside the exam room, before her death of a prescription drug overdose on Feb. 8, 2007.

Although the Medical Board of California launched a review of Dr. Kapoor for prescribing methadone to Smith under a pseudonym in the eighth month of her pregnancy, he was acquitted on all legal counts in Smith’s death and allowed to continue his medical practice.

Penn found during prep for the Briarcliff film that “the real Sandeep was, to my surprise, very welcoming in letting me shadow him, follow him around.”

“I had dinner with him tons of times, and I think through that, saw a couple of things that made me think. There are things that he does physically. He sits differently based on who he’s with. If it’s somebody he’s clearly nervous in front of, he sits very differently than friends or family he’s comfortable with. His manner of speaking and his flamboyance also, not that he’s code-switching, but they clearly switch based on who he’s around,” he added.

Telling Kapoor’s story of his experience with Anna Nicole also involved a “guerrilla style” scene filmed in the middle of the 2024 West Hollywood Pride Parade, made to look like WeHo in 2005.

“Thane, our director, basically had 30 background artists surrounding this car, and it, shot-for-shot, needed to look like the real parade that Anna and Sandeep went on, so everything else in the background is mostly out of focus, unless you could get away with the few things that are remaining from 20 years ago, like Circus of Books,” Penn noted. “But it was super interesting because you also only had one shot, right? You start at the beginning of the parade and you go through to the end and hope that you get everything you need.”

And while Larry Birkhead, the father of Anna Nicole’s daughter Dannielynn, has expressed his disapproval of the project, Penn concedes that it’s “not gonna be a movie for everybody,” but acknowledges that “somebody tragically died, and I would never want to make light of something like that in a film.”

With a busy year coming to a close, which included a “fun” arc as “a terrible person” in Season 4 of BBC/HBO’s Industry , Penn is getting ready to return to his roots following last year’s news of a fourth Harold & Kumar in the works from writers Jon Hurwitz, Hayden Schlossberg and Josh Heald.

“So, John Cho and I have formally signed on for a fourth film,” confirmed Penn. “Jon and Hayden, the amazing screenwriters who’ve written all three movies, they directed the second one, they will direct the fourth one, and they just finished the script, which John and I both read a couple of weeks ago, and I loved it. It tracks with the other three movies, and I’m not just saying this because I play the guy, but it’s one of the funniest scripts that I’ve read in a very long time.”

Penn added, “So I’m excited, but it hasn’t yet been greenlit or anything, so I don’t have any actual updates, other than that I read the script and loved it. So hopefully, we get to make the thing.”

Meanwhile, Penn has been busy checking off a bucket list item after working with New Queer Cinema director Gregg Araki on his next film, The Decline of Fucking Western Civilization , a role he told his agent to “aggressively pursue” after he first saw Araki speak after a UCLA screening of his 1995 film Doom Generation during Penn’s undergrad years.

“I didn’t know anything about the film, you just kind of walk in. I’m like, ‘This is unlike anything I’d ever seen before.’ And then listening to his Q&A about his kind of guerrilla-style filmmaking and shooting in LA and just doing things the way that he always has done—” recalled Penn. “So, I was thrilled to join the cast, and I just wrapped.”

Read on about Kal Penn’s experience playing Dr. Sandeep Kapoor in Trust Me, I’m a Doctor , now in theaters, as well as his upcoming roles in Harold & Kumar 4 , Gregg Araki’s The Decline of Fucking Western Civilization and more.

DEADLINE: What was it about this perspective of Anna Nicole’s story that appealed to you?

KAL PENN: So, I didn’t know very much about her story, and if I’m being honest, I still don’t, because the arc of playing Sandeep in the film is kind of start-to-finish from before he meets Anna to after her passing. And so, I never did the research into her, cause it just made it easier to be Sandeep. And then you wrap a film, and you’re like, “OK, that was it.” … But the reason I said yes to the movie, I remember being a young actor in LA, at the nascent days of reality TV, and I think there was one party I went to, like an awards show, that Anna was at, but she was there with like four cameras and a huge entourage, and it was clear she was shooting a reality show. But I remember my friends and I were like, “Oh, does she have a reality show because that’s how she actually behaves, or is she behaving that way because she has a reality show?” And that’s a question that the film doesn’t fully answer either, it’s an open question by the end of our movie. But that’s all I knew about her, right? It’s like, “Oh yeah, that’s Anna Nicole Smith from that reality show.” So, I see the email come in from my agent for this movie, and it was a short logline that I just skimmed, and then the script was attached. And as I’m clicking on the script, I think to myself like, “Oh yeah, I know this story. This is about that doctor who’s in prison for murdering Anna Nicole Smith.” And then I started reading the script, I was like, “This is not at all what happened. How do I think that’s what happened?” I never followed the case or anything, but why do I think that’s what happened? And then I was like, “Am I one of these people who reads three tweets and thinks I’m an expert on something?” So, I read the script with that in my head and was really fascinated mostly with the insecurity of the character of Sandeep, and the vulnerability and this push and pull between—I think five times in the movie, he says, “I’m just a private person, living a private life,” but then makes every decision contrary to that, just to get attention, right? So, there was that kind of juiciness to a character that I hadn’t played before that attracted me to it.

DEADLINE: What was it like undergoing the physical transformation and changing your voice for the role?

PENN: So obviously, Anna Nicole Smith was in the public eye as a character. Sandeep is an interesting character to play because he wasn’t. I guess he was in the public eye, and therefore fair game and all of that, but he’s not like a household name, and I think the biggest decision in trying to figure out with Thane, our writer-director, about the right way to play him was like, “I just need to ground these vulnerabilities, and these poor ethical decisions in something bigger than what’s on the script,” and the real Sandeep was, to my surprise, very welcoming in letting me shadow him, follow him around. I had dinner with him tons of times, and I think through that, saw a couple of things that made me think. There are things that he does physically. He sits differently based on who he’s with. If it’s somebody he’s clearly nervous in front of, he sits very differently than friends or family he’s comfortable with. His manner of speaking and his flamboyance also, not that he’s code-switching, but they clearly switch based on who he’s around. So, there was a bit of Alexander Technique, there was a bit of backstory to ground all of that, but that’s kind of what went into the transformation. It isn’t necessary because for me, it made a lot of sense, some of the things that you kind of learn about him based on all that.

DEADLINE: It’s funny you bring that up because that was one part of it that I really resonated with, his experience as a closeted gay man, and that one scene at the West Hollywood Pride Parade really made me happy, just seeing that through his eyes, not just befriending Anna Nicole, but being around all of these people who accept him for him, and I’m curious what was it like for you filming that scene?

PENN: That scene is an interesting one, especially hearing your take on it, because in reality, Sandeep told me he had been to the Abbey tons of times with his friends, always had a great time, but generally felt invisible in that space. So, guys weren’t coming up to him to strike up a conversation. Some of that may have been because he’s a nerdy brown doctor, and Weho at that time especially was fairly homogeneous, the standard of beauty was very different. It still is like that, but thankfully less so compared to 20 years ago. So, what he had told me, and this actually ties into an earlier part of getting to know him a little bit, when I shadowed him for the first time, something clicked. I went to his office, it’s still in the Valley, same office as before, it’s small. And when you go in, there are like three receptionists, and his little waiting room, and then maybe three exam rooms. Glenn, I don’t know about you, but when I make an appointment to see my doctor, I either talk to a fucking AI slop bot that makes my blood boil, or I have to log in and pick a slot. And in both cases, there’s no appointments for like seven and a half weeks. So, when I saw the way that Sandeep works, and there’s a human who picks up the phone and he knows all of his patients … it was that 1950s personal touch of doing medicine that immediately made me recognize, “OK, it’s not weird that Anna invited him to Pride,” because it was common for him to get invitations to somebody’s bar mitzvah, or your patient’s Super Bowl party. Those were just things that would happen. So, when Anna invited him to the Pride Parade and then to the Abbey, it made sense that he would go. What didn’t make sense is, you could have two champagnes with your patient/acquaintance. Don’t have nine bottles of champagne with her, and then don’t make out with her on the couch next to the dance floor. These are objectively horrendous decisions, right? So, I think knowing all of that and then knowing in the real world, this was very grounding for me, knowing that the real Sandeep had been to the Abbey and enjoyed it, but the way he was experiencing it through the lens of Anna, it was clear to him that he was getting tons of attention from all of these people, because he was in her proximity and her orbit, and he knew that wasn’t real for him. But it was so intoxicating for the night, that to me that was fun, it was tragic, it was heartbreaking. It was also no sympathy for somebody who’s making bad decisions. It was all of those things, it was a night at the Abbey, you know?

DEADLINE: Yeah. Did y’all actually shoot at the Abbey?

PENN: No, we shot most of the movie in Toronto, so this was a nondescript club in Toronto. The only stuff we shot in the States, in LA, was the Pride Parade stuff.

DEADLINE: Yeah, I was gonna say I saw y’all going past Circus of Books. Was it actually filmed during the Pride Parade?

PENN: Yeah, it was guerrilla style, so Thane, our director, basically had 30 background artists surrounding this car, and it, shot-for-shot, needed to look like the real parade that Anna and Sandeep went on, so everything else in the background is mostly out of focus, unless you could get away with the few things that are remaining from 20 years ago, like Circus of Books, so that’s why you got a good shot of that. but it was super interesting because you also only had one shot, right? You start at the beginning of the parade and you go through to the end and hope that you get everything you need.

DEADLINE: What was it like shooting the make-out/vomit scene, cause that seems like it could have gone wrong.

PENN: It was fun. I mean, it was one of those scenes that it’s like 7:30 in the morning in a dingy club in Toronto. I know the story that everybody wants to hear is, “Was it late at night and were you guys having a good time?” Yes, we were having a good time. It’s just like, first up after brushing your teeth, you get to puke.

DEADLINE: It broke my heart that he was forced to publicly come out in order to save his career, but it did make me happy when he finally came out to his dad. Tell me about exploring that dynamic.

PENN: It’s funny, a lot of people are asking about that dynamic. I think it’s interesting because it’s not as compelling to me as the horrific decisions that he made. I know why we have it in the script, because you need something personal to flavor this. Otherwise, it’s a legal drama, but the parts that drove the stuff that maybe culminates with the scene with his dad, there are multiple scenes that I have with Linda Hamilton, where I, as Sandeep, am withholding critical legal information from my defense lawyer, which is like, “Why would you do that?” And it shows you the psychology of, he thinks that he’s doing the right thing. So no matter what missteps he’s making, and I think now having it out there and audiences seeing it, watching it, going, “Do not make this decision, I’m watching a train wreck, I’m passing a car accident on the 405, I know it’s gonna be bad. I know you’re making this decision. I wish you wouldn’t—yep, there you go, you did it.” It’s like, understanding why he does that, he thinks it’s gonna be the right thing. I remember asking him, “Why did you take the files home from your office?” And hindsight… Sandeep’s like, “It’s two things. One, I probably shouldn’t have, clearly.” But he had paparazzi posing as patients, coming into his office, trying to get appointments with him. And he genuinely believed that they were gonna come in, break in in the middle of the night, and steal Anna’s files, and all of her medical information would get out there. And I was just like, “Yeah, but the only other choice was to take home the files?” I’m like, “Bro, this does not add up. Those are not the only two choices in life, right?” So to me, it’s the way that he talks himself into this circle of poor decision-making that I never considered were for him, a lie on a lie on a lie. And I think in exploring the relationship with his dad, you can see the weight that had on him. In real life, if I’m remembering this correctly, the real Sandeep was very open with his mom and with all of his friends, and so, crafting that relationship with the dad and the parents was, I think for Thane, a little bit more of a creative liberty for the film. It’s also why I think I gravitate so much towards the bad decisions that he made with his vulnerability as opposed to any of the identity stuff, whether it’s ethnic identity or sexuality or anything like that.

DEADLINE: I’m curious if you happen to have seen Larry Birkhead’s response ?

PENN: I did, yeah.

DEADLINE: What were your thoughts?

PENN: You know, I didn’t really have thoughts on it, only because I think I was so hyper-focused on trying to bring Sandeep to life. I also know very little about the real Anna Nicole Smith. I think the one thing that that was important to me was, somebody tragically died, and I would never want to make light of something like that in a film. So, I remember asking Thane, I was like, “This is kind of being pitched as a dark comedy. I hope the comedy is not in the tragic passing of this woman.” He’s like, “No, no, no, of course not.” And then you read the script and you see the dark comedy comes from the self-deprecation of Sandeep. But of course, I mean, people will have their opinions on it. It’s not gonna be a movie for everybody, and so if there are folks who feel like this is disturbing for any reason, I’m not the guy who’s like, “You should see it anyway.” You should skip this one.

DEADLINE: I know that someone was talking about a fourth Harold and Kumar not too long ago. Is that happening?

PENN: Yeah. … So, John Cho and I have formally signed on for a fourth film, which I think Deadline reported on a couple of months ago. Jon [Hurwitz] and Hayden [Schlossberg], the amazing screenwriters who’ve written all three movies, they directed the second one, they will direct the fourth one, and they just finished the script, which John and I both read a couple of weeks ago, and I loved it. It tracks with the other three movies, and I’m not just saying this because I play the guy, but it’s one of the funniest scripts that I’ve read in a very long time. … You kind of can’t make a movie like this unless it sticks with the satire and the reflection of what’s happening in the world, in a way that only I think Jon Hurwitz and Hayden Schlossberg can write, and I just thought it was so smartly done with the appropriate amount of the dumb jokes that always come with the Harold & Kumar movie, so I’m excited, but it hasn’t yet been greenlit or anything, so I don’t have any actual updates, other than that I read the script and loved it. So hopefully, we get to make the thing. I usually text them once every two and a half, three weeks to be like, “Any updates?” So, I will do that this afternoon.

DEADLINE: I love the franchise, and I’m curious, are you and John Cho down to keep this franchise going to the grave? We see Cheech and Chong still out there, kicking it.

PENN: You’d have to ask John for his thoughts. I can tell you that over the years, I think after the starting with the second movie, I was basically like, “My gosh, what good fortune do I have to be able to make these kinds of things?” I had loved comedy before, obviously not to compare Harold & Kumar to something that I revere, but one of the things I loved about the writing from the Jon and Hayden brains was that it almost reminded me of … one of the reasons that I loved the Muppets, and never shed my love for the Muppets in the years since, is that some of the early Muppet movies, there are jokes that are clearly in there for the adults in the room, and then there’s the other stuff for the kids. And I think that what they do with these movies is, if you just wanna walk in and laugh with your friends, which is really the goal ultimately, satire and commentary aside, the number one goal of these things is always to just make anybody laugh. You laugh and you leave happy with your friends, and if you wanna find the satire in it and you like that, that’s obviously in there for you too. So, I just sort of loved that and was like, “I feel lucky to begin with that we made, we got to make three of them. I’d be very happy if we made 50 of them before I died.” I just think that the character is also so much cooler than I will ever be, and especially as the world has gotten more and more polarized, it’s one of the things I love about those characters is that it means a lot to me. I’ve talked to Jon and Hayden about this, and they feel the same way. It means a lot to us that people enjoy it across the political spectrum, and that’s been very cool, that in a world in which we have relatively few things that we can do together anymore, I like that food, comedy, movies, music, those are still things that can kind of have that magic, and that’s been very cool to see also.

DEADLINE: Well, as a gay stoner who went to Harold & Kumar in theaters when I was in middle school, I’m looking forward to the next one.

PENN: Oh, thank you. OK, you’re a gay stoner—I just wrapped this Gregg Araki movie yesterday.

DEADLINE: I love Gregg. You’re working with him on The Decline of Fucking Western Civilization ? Awesome title. How did you come onto the project?

PENN: So, I signed with Anonymous Content recently, and my manager basically reached out. It was like, “There’s a role in the new Gregg Araki movie—” and I like interrupted it, but I was like, “OK, let’s go ahead and make that happen.” He’s like, “Well, I’m sending you the script, and here’s all the details for the meetings and the all of that.” It was one of those things, it almost sounds cliche, but I was like, “I mean, obviously I will read it, but I can tell you right now I would like to aggressively pursue this.” And part of the reason was, the first movie I saw when I moved out to LA, I did undergrad at UCLA, and it was literally the first week of theater and film school. There was a Doom Generation screening on campus, and Gregg and the cast came to do a panel and a Q&A. And I didn’t know anything about the film, you just kind of walk in. I’m like, “This is unlike anything I’d ever seen before.” And then listening to his Q&A about his kind of guerrilla style filmmaking and shooting in LA and just doing things the way that he always has done—which when I talked to him about this movie, I obviously told him that story. But he’s like, “You know, I always shoot in LA. I’ve never shot anywhere else.” And he’s just sort of walking you through the things that I guess I knew as a Gregg Araki fan, but it was very cool to actually hear. So, I was thrilled to join the cast, and I just wrapped.

DEADLINE: You’ve been doing a lot of really cool roles lately, and I was also curious about joining Industry for Season 4. What was it like working with those guys?

PENN: That was awesome. Mickey [Down] and Konrad [Kay] are two of the smartest and most insane writers. Every script that we had, I was like, “This is amazing. I can’t believe I get to do and say this.” I don’t know what most actors say, but I’ll tell you, I always feel like, playing a terrible person is way more fun than than playing somebody who’s good. And so, the Industry world, I was a fan of before, because it’s a world that I don’t actually know personally, but the scripts and the storylines were so insane that that was another one where that kind of offer came through, and I was super excited. It turned out that both of them are actually big Harold & Kuma r fans, which is how I guess my name entered their psyche for this particular role. And I loved that they kind of counter-cast it, like Kumar is this wonderfully gregarious, friendly guy who’s everybody’s best friend, and the Jonah character I play in Industry is very much the opposite, incredibly flawed, womanizing, misogynistic, greed-fueled, at least you think so until you realize he also got fucked over by Max Minghella’s character. But I had the best time making that. We were in London and Cardiff for I guess about two months last year, and those are the kind of writers where they’re so smart—to me, that show is not binge-able because it’s so dark, in the same way that Succession was not binge-able for me, which is a testament to how good it is, where it’s like I need a week or two between episodes to sit with this. I need to sit with it and think about it. But then, the rewatch rate for me is super high also, where I’ll go back and catch things that I hadn’t caught the first time. Just kind of placing a lot of those things in the work when you’re doing that was great. And most of my scenes were with Max Minghella, who I just think the world of. What a phenomenal actor and director.

DEADLINE: But I know your character Jonah might have an ax to grind. Do you think he could potentially come back for Season 5?

PENN: I would love if he did. I don’t know if he will. Look, I’ll take him if he comes back. I definitely think he left with a huge ax to grind, and the last scene that you see him in is just wasted at a strip club in Miami, so who knows where he goes? But you know what, let me pitch him, to throw this one out there. He he could do a spin-off. That’d be fine… I mean, that’s not a real thing.

DEADLINE: Let’s just manifest it.

PENN: Sure, sure, I’d do that. My point is, it’s rare to have kind of all those layers and that darkness to a world. Prepping for that, I remember texting either Mickey or Konrad. I was like, “Hey, I’m walking around. I had a list of places where bankers go in London, Canary Wharf. What’s a good bar if I wanna just listen and eavesdrop on conversations with bankers?” And they’re like, “Why would you do that? Go have a nice fucking meal at Chiltern Firehouse. Don’t.” I was like, “No, no, no, guys. Come on, I’m not method, but I’ve got this week to immerse myself in this insanity.” I just think they’re so thoughtful, they know that world really well, but they’re not restricted by it. The friends I talked to who work in that world, they’re like, “Yeah, a lot of that stuff comes from a very real place.” It’s clear that they had spent time there before crafting these characters, and so, as somebody with very little business sense, I just love a good nerdy deep dive into character background and what the hell I’m actually doing, learning all the terms. … I love the research that goes into it. And so, for something like Industry , even for a half-season arc, it was cool to just be fully immersive and kind of learn as much about that world as possible, to bring that shady dude to life.

DEADLINE: I know you have a few other upcoming projects. Can you say anything about Contra or What the Fuck Is My Password ?

PENN: Yeah, What the Fuck Is My Password is very funny. It’s basically about, a guy who essentially loses a crypto password, and things that happen to him after that. I’ll be vague because I can’t remember how much they put out there, but it was very funny. We shot that in New Jersey. And then Contra is this super dark, almost like a 1980s style chess thriller that’s based on—I didn’t know that this was real. There are these underground chess competitions called Contra, where basically these really good world-class chess players will get a shady sponsor who has to drop like $100,000 as an entry fee, for example, to these underground competitions, in the hopes that they also will then recoup most of the winnings, go to the person who invested in the entry fee for this contestant. So, this is a movie about the underworld of that and the greed. So, I play a not nice guy. I play one of the gangsters who’s kind of controlling one of these Contra chess organizations. It was very cool. We shot in Bangkok last year, and I think they’re wrapping up post now. But it was interesting, the movie doesn’t take place in Bangkok, so it was one of those tax benefit things that I guess the producers felt like that was the best place to shoot. But the crews are fantastic. It’s definitely a grittier feel. I haven’t seen the rough cut yet, but at least what they were going for stylistically was the Rambo , Terminator , late 1980s, early 1990s kind of feel. So visually, I think it’ll look pretty wild.

title_original: 二宮和也、エイミー・ホンマ、村田千恵子が日本映画の未来を語る。ケリング「ウーマン・イン・モーション」トーク開催
editorial_title_zh: 二宫和也、艾米·本间、村田千惠子共谈日本电影未来。开云集团“跃动她影”（Women in Motion）对谈活动即将举办
editorial_excerpt_zh: 全球奢侈品集团开云将于2026年10月27日作为第39届东京国际电影节的官方赞助活动举办“跃动她影”（Women in Motion）对谈。今年是该项目创立的第11年，也是引入日本举办的第9年
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "全球奢侈品集团开云将于2026年10月27日作为第39届东京国际电影节的官方赞助活动举办“跃动她影”（Women in Motion）对谈。今年是该项目创立的第11年，也是引入日本举办的第9年。目前正在公开招募观众，截止时间为9月30日。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今年，在电影导演是枝裕和发表开场致辞之后，奥斯卡电影博物馆馆长兼总裁、兼任学院藏品总负责人的艾米·本间，歌手兼演员二宫和也，以及曾参与电影《国宝》（2025）策划与制片的电影制片人村田千惠子将登台。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "宏观俯瞰世界电影文化的本间、将日本电影推向世界的村田，以及积累了国内外电影制作现场经验的二宫。他们将分别从“传承与发扬电影文化的立场”、“孕育作品的立场”以及“诠释作品的立场”出发，围绕日本电影的魅力与可能性、在世界之中的当前定位以及面向下一代的电影文化应有形态展开讨论。此外，还将从性别、多元性以及盟友关系（allyship）的视角，探讨培育创造力的环境。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本间于2024年就任奥斯卡金像奖主办方美国电影艺术与科学学院在洛杉矶建立的奥斯卡电影博物馆馆长兼总裁。目前，她不仅统筹该馆的展览、放映及教育项目等，还负责管理超过5200万件的奥斯卡藏品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "二宫曾出演克林特·伊斯特ウッド导演的《来自硫磺岛的信》（2006），并主演了在第78届戛纳国际电影节上进行世界首映的《8番出口》（2025）等作品，作为演员在国内外活跃。村田在参与制作《王者天下》（2019）等作品后，策划并制作了于2025年上映的《国宝》。该片在戛纳国际电影节“导演双周”单元进行世界首映，并获得了第98届奥斯卡金像奖最佳化妆与发型设计奖提名。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对谈结束后，将特别放映由劳伦·王（Lulu Wang）导演的《别告诉她》（2019），这也是本间所选出的对自己产生影响的具有突破性的美国真人电影之一。该片取材于身为美籍华裔导演的王自身的经历，描绘了亚裔移民的身份认同与家庭。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "开云集团的“跃动她影”（Women in Motion）于2015年在与戛纳国际电影节的合作下启动，旨在聚焦电影界无论镜头内外活跃女性的创造力与成就。如今，其视线已不仅局限于性别，更扩展至包括文化背景和种族等在内的多样化声音，并发展成为旨在实现更具包容性文化环境的国际性倡议。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "开云集团“跃动她影”（Women in Motion）对谈 日期：2026年10月27日（周二）13:30〜16:40（暂定） 会场：TOHO CINEMAS 六本木新城 银幕7 票务：免费 报名：开云“跃动她影”官方LINE账号（https://lin.ee/smRUyo8） 名额：60名 报名期间：9月17日（周四）8:00〜9月30日（周三）23:59 ※如报名人数过多将进行抽签", "translated": true}]

article_text:
グローバル・ラグジュアリー・グループのケリングが、2026年10月27日、第39回東京国際映画祭 提携企画として「ウーマン・イン・モーション」トークを開催する。プログラム創設から11年目、日本での開催は9年目を迎える。現在9月30日まで観覧者を募集中だ。

今年は、映画監督・是枝裕和によるオープニング・スピーチに続き、アカデミー・ミュージアム・オブ・モーション・ピクチャーズ館長兼プレジデントで、アカデミー・コレクション統括責任者のエイミー・ホンマ、歌手・俳優の二宮和也、映画『国宝』（2025）の企画・プロデュースを手がけた映画プロデューサーの村田千恵子が登壇。

世界の映画文化を俯瞰するホンマ、日本映画を世界へ届けてきた村田、国内外の映画制作現場を経験してきた二宮。それぞれ「映画文化を継承・発信する立場」「作品を生み出す立場」「作品を体現する立場」から、日本映画の魅力や可能性、世界から見た現在地、次世代へ向けた映画文化のあり方について議論する。さらに、ジェンダー、多様性、アライシップの観点から、創造性を育む環境についても考える。

ホンマは2024年、アカデミー賞を主催する映画芸術科学アカデミーがロサンゼルスに設立したアカデミー・ミュージアムの館長兼プレジデントに就任。現在は同館の展覧会や上映、教育プログラムなどに加え、5200万点を超えるアカデミー・コレクションを統括している。

二宮はクリント・イーストウッド監督『硫黄島からの手紙』（2006）への出演をはじめ、第78回カンヌ国際映画祭でワールドプレミアされた『8番出口』（2025）に主演するなど、国内外で俳優として活動。村田は『キングダム』（2019）などの製作を経て、2025年公開の『国宝』を企画・プロデュースした。同作はカンヌ国際映画祭「監督週間」でワールドプレミアされ、第98回アカデミー賞メイクアップ＆ヘアスタイリング部門にノミネートされた。

トーク終了後には、ホンマが自身に影響を与えた画期的なアメリカ実写映画のひとつとして選んだ、ルル・ワン監督『フェアウェル』（2019）を特別上映。中国系アメリカ人監督であるワン自身の体験をもとに、アジア系移民のアイデンティティと家族を描いた作品だ。

ケリング「ウーマン・イン・モーション」は2015年、カンヌ国際映画祭とのパートナーシップのもと、映画界でカメラの前後を問わず活躍する女性の創造性と功績に光を当てるプログラムとしてスタート。現在ではジェンダーだけでなく、文化的背景や人種などを含む多様な声へと視点を広げ、よりインクルーシブな文化環境を目指す国際的な取り組みへ発展している。

ケリング「ウーマン・イン・モーション」トーク 日時：2026年10月27日（火）13:30〜16:40（予定） 会場：TOHOシネマズ 六本木ヒルズ スクリーン7 入場料：無料 申込：ケリング「ウーマン・イン・モーション」公式LINEアカウント（https://lin.ee/smRUyo8） 定員：60名 申込期間：9月17日（木）8:00〜9月30日（水）23:59 ※応募多数の場合は抽選

article_text:
Source: AFM

Fairmont Century Plaza in Lose Angeles

This is a pivotal time for independent production and, on the eve of the American Film Market (AFM, November 10-15), US attendees in Los Angeles will be eager to examine fundamental developments that could shape the future of the industry.

The corridors of the Fairmont Century Plaza and surrounding venues will be humming with discussion around David Ellison’s $111bn merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery, which has already irked the community due to a perceived lack of protections for the independent space. In September, independent producers lambasted provisions in the five-year consent decree thrashed out between Ellison’s negotiators and California attorney general Rob Bonta that averted an antitrust trial and paved the way for the merger.

The decree stipulated that the new combined company Skydance will release four ‘independent’ films a year within an annual slate of at least 30 in the first two years and 32 in the following three. It also specified that within 30 days of the merger closing on October 6, Skydance would set up an independent acquisition fund allocating $5m per year over five years.

Skydance has not said who would lead the fund at press time, although Lia Buman, who headed Paramount’s global acquisitions team and Republic Pictures prior to the merger, was seen as a likely candidate. However, there has been much grumbling over the allocation, which independents regard as a paltry sum given market realities. After all, Focus Features spent around $15m buying Obsession in Toronto last year.

Yet even though the consent decree is largely viewed by the independent community as a toothless cave-in by Bonta, whom they suspect bowed to political pressure to get the deal over the line, the loose definitions of ‘independent’ and the requirement on Skydance to produce or co-produce only 50% of its annual output means it will be looking to buy films to make up the numbers. That is an opportunity independent producers and sales agents want to explore.

Meanwhile, the freshly minted American Entertainment Alliance (AEA), an umbrella group comprising producers, US agencies and independent outfits such as Blumhouse and MRC, is pushing for a revival of the old Hollywood Financial Interest and Syndication Rules, or ‘fin-syn’, which restricted leading networks of the day from owning everything they broadcast, until the rules were eliminated in 1995. AEA members want to push for legislation to enact an updated version that would essentially require streamers with a minimum of 10 million US subscribers to allocate half of their original content spend on independent film and television. That would give a significant leg-up to the independents at a time when pay-1 output deals are thin on the ground. The streamers are pushing back.

Another major development that will inform AFM conversations around packaging is the proposed US federal production incentive, a 20% transferable tax credit that can be combined with state incentives. The measure has drawn rare bipartisan support under the Trump administration and could pass into law by early next year, if not sooner. It is universally supported within Hollywood.

Fairmont fare

AFM attendees will be digesting and debating all this as they participate in the last major market of the year, coming less than two months after the inaugural TIFF: The Market, which by and large did not change how industry professionals did business in Toronto.

FilmNation attends AFM with a roster of sales titles that had not been unveiled at press time, and will continue talks on Bill Hader’s upcoming psychological horror They Know . The team showed first footage in Toronto, where FilmNation stayed away from the official TIFF: The Market footprint and engaged in sales activity as it always does north of the border — on an opportunistic, more modest basis than at AFM or Cannes. It also introduced MRC’s queer romantic comedy Honeymoon/Funeral starring Rebecca Ferguson and Greta Lee, selling North American rights to Black Bear.

In a strong year for the company, The Invite , a film it sold and served on as a producer, has embedded itself in awards conversations and continues to open around the world, debuting in Spain last month. Olivia Wilde’s adult comedy has grossed more than $60m at the global box office on a budget of less than $15m and is an example of the kind of elevated fare that strikes a chord.

Source: FilmNation Entertainment

Alice Laffile

“Buyers, at least at the pre-sales stage, are looking for distinctive, filmmaker-driven projects that have a clear creative identity and know exactly what type of audiences they’re targeting,” says FilmNation senior vice president of sales Alice Laffillé. “Buyers are more cautious and the price tag matters. We’re trying to find the balance between what our filmmakers are looking for and the right platforms for them to make their movies, and a way for independent buyers to afford those films.”

Finding that balance is not easy. “Right now, most independent films of any scale are comparatively expensive to make, difficult to market and have too unpredictable a revenue model,” says AGC Studios founder and CEO Stuart Ford. The executive hopes technological developments and a stackable US federal incentive will help to lower costs. “Within the next few years we might be looking at net production exposures that are at least 20%-25% lower than they are currently.”

AGC will commence sales talks on completed sci-fi epic Gods Don’t Give Gifts , an AI-rendered animation from YouTuber Zack London (aka Gossip Goblin). The film will screen to buyers and ‘superfans’ on the first day of the market. AGC will also show footage from post-­production titles such as Fleur starring Halle Berry, family animation Critterz and Spooky Pictures’ psychological thriller Sundowning .

Ford and his team took offices at the InterContinental in Toronto, one of two hotels affiliated to the market, and reported a productive trip. They sold Lauren Miller Rogen’s comedy and TIFF world premiere Babies starring Anna Kendrick and Seth Rogen, and showed first footage from The Last Druid . “There’s room for both a Toronto market and AFM to be useful and necessary touchstones for a community that’s increasingly in dialogue and sharing materials all year round,” insists Ford.

“The domestic market is not doing as great as it used to and that does affect the international market,” says Palisades Park Pictures CEO Tamara Birkemoe, who is fielding offers on Bill Condon’s musical drama The Road Home starring Cynthia Erivo, and hopes to have footage ready to show by the Berlinale following a summer shoot.

“Buyers must feel like they have to have the project in order to get engaged and involved and make decent offers. People are still active and still want theatrical movies, they’re just being more picky.”

Change in demand

Source: Highland Film Group

Emile Hirsch and Annamarie Kasper in ‘Lice’

Marc Goldberg, co-founder of distributor Aura Entertainment, says buying has become “more and more a science rather than a gut feeling, like it used to be”. The company — launched in 2025 by Goldberg’s UK distributor Signature Entertainment, Christian Mercuri’s Capstone Studios and Jared Goetz’s Ascending Media — targets 12-15 commercial titles a year and tailors releases from wide theatrical to straight-to-streaming.

“The narrowness of revenue earning just means that you have to be working that much more closely with the demands of the audience and the streamers,” says Goldberg, who released Renny Harlin’s action thriller The Beast starring Samuel L Jackson in theatres last month. “You’ve seen the success of Obsession and we’re forever looking for that next gem. We know first-hand what can be achieved.” (Curry Barker’s horror smash was produced by Capstone and initially intended to open through Aura before the partners opted to sell in Toronto.)

Source: Highland Film Group

Todd Olsson

For all but those rarest of titles that can spark bidding wars, the post-Covid rhythm of deal-making and buyer caution means that sellers need to be patient. “You need a couple of strong markets to get enough pre-sales to push it over the line in terms of financing,” notes Todd Olsson, president of international sales at Highland Film Group.

He will screen Justin Chadwick’s spy thriller The Mark with Jessica Alba, Tom Hopper and Elsa Pataky, and debut director Jonathan Bensimon’s 1980s-set parasite horror Lice starring Emile Hirsch and Justin Long. In Toronto, Highland introduced buyers to true-life comedy The Fun Lady , which will see Andy Tennant direct Alba, and Nimrod Antal’s sci-fi action thriller Bluefly starring Russell Crowe and Priyanka Chopra Jonas, scheduled to start production in Australia later this year.

TIFF was fruitful for Highland, although Olsson knows not all the buyers from Europe who attended can justify a trip to AFM, or vice versa. “It’s difficult for some of them to come to North America twice within a six-week period, especially the way air travel is now and the cost of hotels and food. They have to choose.”

Screen digital edition: November 2026
